sources.title: Regione Sardegna: the age of the giudicati
sources.note: Official regional synthesis. Four kingdoms securely attested by the middle eleventh century; avoid treating their earlier emergence as a precisely dated event.

sources.title: Italian Ministry of Culture: the abandoned medieval village of Geridu
sources.note: Account contributed by excavation director Marco Milanese, Museo Biddas. Paragraphs 1 to 3: documentary dates, settlement and household spaces.

sources.title: Francesca Montichiara: women in giudicale Sardinia through the condaghi
sources.note: University of Sassari doctoral research, printed pp. 9, 71 to 72; direct full PDF inspected. Property records include institutional bias and unfree people, not a portrait of universal female autonomy.

sources.title: Regione Sardegna: the Carta de Logu
sources.note: Late-fourteenth-century promulgation, civil/criminal/rural components and continued use until April 1827. Avoid uncritical claims of modern equality.

sources.title: Scano di Montiferro municipal educational collection: Carta de Logu excerpts
sources.note: I nostri passi 1, printed p. 65 / PDF index 64: modern transcription of prologue with Italian translation; printed pp. 66 to 67 / PDF indices 65 to 66: articles 86 and 87. Screenshot service failed, full PDF text and indexed page witness checked.

sources.title: Regione Sardegna: the church of the Holy Trinity at Saccargia
sources.note: Official architectural history: Camaldolese possession from 1112, two-tone stonework and Romanesque apse frescoes. Founding vision explicitly a legend and omitted.

sources.title: Regione Sardegna: Iglesias and its walls
sources.note: Urban/mining history; 1308 descriptions of defenses; seven-month siege ending 14 January 1324.

sources.title: Regione Sardegna: the Battle of Sanluri
sources.note: 30 June 1409 defeat, 1410 capitulation and 17 August 1420 sale of remaining dynastic rights. Army totals omitted.

sources.title: Centro di Studi Filologici Sardi: historical chronology of Sardinia
sources.note: Entries 1527 to 1720 checked. Spanish crown phase followed by Austrian rule in 1708, Spanish return in 1717 and Savoy possession in 1720. Do not equate 1700 coverage end with immediate political termination.

sources.title: Italian archival administration: the military estate of the Kingdom of Sardinia
sources.note: SIUSA institutional history, substantive paragraphs 1 to 8. Estate composition, bargaining and separate meeting places.

sources.title: Regione Sardegna Virtual Archaeology: the coastal tower system
sources.note: 1587 Royal Administration, garrisons and elevated entrances. General tower-system descriptions span its continuing operation; avoid assigning late gun totals to a precise sixteenth-century year.

sources.title: University of Cagliari: original foundation documents
sources.note: Luisa D’Arienzo account of 1607 papal bull, 1620 royal privilege, municipal finance and 1626 implementation; direct page checked. Attached transcription link failed, so not used for writing sample.

sources.title: University Library of Cagliari: sixteenth-century books
sources.note: Official library original indexed result confirms Nicolò Canelles established printing shop in Cagliari in 1566; direct fetch failed. No assertion that every earlier claimed Sardinian printing is impossible.

sources.title: Maurizio Virdis: introduction to Araolla’s Rimas diversas spirituales
sources.note: Critical edition, Centro di Studi Filologici Sardi/CUEC 2006. Printed pp. XI to XII schooling and 1567 Castilian requirement; p. XVII trilingual collection; p. CXVI confirms 1597 publication.

sources.title: Maurizio Virdis: the surviving 1597 printing of Araolla
sources.note: Printed pp. CLXXI to CLXXII, PDF indices 0 to 1, identifies sole surviving 1597 copy Biblioteca Universitaria di Cagliari S.P. 6.10.2; quotes exact uppercase title on original p. 17. Sample is three-word title, translated literally as Various spiritual poems.

sources.title: Bianucci and colleagues: Angelerio and plague control in Alghero
sources.note: Emerging Infectious Diseases 19(9), 2013, 1478 to 1483. Primary historical reconstruction with contemporary documents. Table 1 is same article and counted under this URL, not a separate budget. Rules are prescriptions, not proof of universal obedience.

sources.title: Milanese, Giuffra and Minozzi: dental health in sixteenth-century Alghero
sources.note: University of Sassari record and original article abstract: 160 examined individuals, 81 adults and 79 subadults; diet inference, not identified recipes. Direct repository fetch failed but original indexed abstract and Pisa-author manuscript abstract both checked. DOI 10.1016/j.archoralbio.2020.104928.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Whole-island imported geometry at 1000, 1100, 1200, 1279, 1300 and 1400; cannot represent a single Kingdom of Sardinia throughout. Narrative explicitly regional and distinguishes four giudicati from later Aragonese consolidation. 1492 is map coverage only. Writing is a modern transcription of the historic prologue, not claimed to be autograph.

Imported geometry is Sardinia island at 1530/1600/1650, map coverage 1530 to 1700. Separate narrative from medieval sardinia and later Piedmont/Savoy kingdom. No claim of destruction in 1700. Towers described as a system with continuing use; general access arrangements not falsely assigned to an exact year. Plague rules and article count as one source budget.
